behaviours.detail: Every hub-linked page ends with three controls (Save and continue | Save and return to overview [exit=hub] | Cancel and return to overview); child pages (collection entry sub-pages, pickers reached from a parent) show the primary alone via showReturnControls=false. exit=hub commits then redirects to the hub, winning over change context and run navigation (kit.exitTarget precedence). Copied verbatim from animals shared/save-actions.njk and shared/kit.js:96; the plants engine already ships save-actions.njk and kit.exitTarget (skeleton change-context-and-exits). Also answers NNS-UN-009 (complete dependably whenever required) and Annex 6 nfr-minimise-trader-effort.

Scope is derived from the manifest on every read and write, never stored; a value whose controlling answer moves it out of scope is purged and never restored (Yes-No-Yes). Every conditional plants obligation is expressed as activatedBy with wipeOnExit=true as the default proposal (commodityType gates arrivalStatus, arrivalTime, proposedPlaceOfLanding, supplierIdentificationNumber, producerIdentificationNumber, cropIdentificationNumber; per-line category gates genus, species, commodityCode, potatoVariety, potatoIntendedUse, eppoCode, sizeOfTree, phytosanitaryTreatments, use). Retain-value (inScope:true + optional on whenFalse) is animals' one exception (regionOfOriginCode) and is not proposed anywhere in plants. Source: skeleton docs/scope-and-wipe.md, model/obligations/evaluator.js, bridge/purge.js; live-animals scope-and-wipe. The wipe-vs-retain choice is a gate question — see conflict on NNS-UN-006 'flexible' and NNS-UN-041 reuse.

Any GET/POST under /notifications/{journeyId}/... except the entry page (and its sub-paths), the create path and the action slugs amend/cancel-amend/copy/delete is admitted only when the opening run has begun for that journey in this session or the journey holds at least one committed USER answer; otherwise redirect to the entry page. The plants entry page is commodity-type (first journey page). flow/entry-guard.js is inert today (async () => null) — restoring it is a declared backlog extra anchored after the commodity-type page because it needs that page's identity. Source: skeleton entry-guard-shape (flow/entry-guard.js:5, routes.js:62-65, set README 'Gates on the first journey-page increment'); live-animals entry-guard.

A Change link on Check your answers goes to the page that collects the obligation with ?change=1; kit.changeContext reads it, kit.withChangeContext carries it through back links, pickers and the commodities list/entry loop, and kit.exitTarget returns the user to notification-view after the save instead of onward. Only the exiting Continue repoints to CYA; mid-loop actions (Save and add another, Remove) never bounce there early. Satisfies annex:6/functional/item:12 'Ability to amend the notification before submitting' and NNS-UN-007. Source: live-animals change-from-cya (shared/kit.js:99); skeleton change-context-and-exits.

The review section (notification-view, declaration, confirmation) is gated by scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers — every task row FULFILLED, NA or OPTIONAL. Declaration is the only flow-only page: one checkbox (value confirmed) whose label is the confirmation sentence, Date of declaration: {today}, Continue; POST commits the flow-only answer then state.submitJourney; success -> SUBMITTED and redirect to confirmation; a not-ok result redirects to CYA; an already-SUBMITTED journey redirects straight to confirmation. submitJourney stamps dateOfNotification and derives lateNotificationIndicator (open question). Source: live-animals declaration-and-submit-gate; skeleton flow-only-keys-declaration, derived-gates.

Start a new notification POSTs /notifications: the record is created (reference minted), beginOpeningRun stores RUN_ACTIVE for that journey, and the user is redirected to commodity-type. While active, kit.nextTarget follows RUN_STEPS in the spec's section order — commodity-type -> commodities -> commodity-details (per line) -> origin -> arrival-status -> arrival-details -> place-of-destination -> consignor-select -> identification-numbers -> consignment-contact-select -> contact-details — skipping any step whose derived gate fails (arrival-status for potatoes; identification-numbers shows only in-scope fields), then lands on the hub, whose GET marks the run complete. A resumed notification navigates section by section from the hub. Run order and sections order are kept identical (animals' ordering quirk is not copied). Source: live-animals opening-run (flow/run.js); skeleton opening-run (run-state.js, kit.js:110-120). Provisional pick under c-034.

The Overview is a govukTaskList per numbered group (1. About the consignment [commodities, origin] | 2. Arrival and destination [arrival, destination] | 3. Consignment parties [consignor, identificationNumbers, contact] | 4. Check and submit [review]). Row status tags: Completed (green), In progress (light blue), Not yet started (blue), Optional (plain text), Cannot start yet (no link). A task row is a submit-readiness unit computed over the union of its pages' collects; rows whose whole content is conditional are marked conditional and hidden when NA (none in plants today — identificationNumbers stays visible as Optional for wood); the review row is Cannot start yet until readyForCheckYourAnswers; each row links to its first gate-passing page; a secondary Return to dashboard button closes the list. The animals totals panel is not copied. Source: live-animals hub-task-list, hub-row-status-rules, hub-linked-conditional-rows; skeleton task-rows-and-readiness, hub-and-check-answers-shape.

Every journey page rendered through kit.base with a journey shows a status strip above the heading: a govukTag Draft (blue) / Submitted (green) / Amending (yellow) / Deleted (grey) followed by the bold reference number (notificationStatus + referenceNumber). Welsh: Drafft / Wedi’i gyflwyno / Wrthi’n diwygio / Wedi’i ddileu. Source: live-animals journey-strip (shared/kit.js:33); the plants engine ships the same kit. Serves annex:6/generated-data/item:1 and item:3 on every page, not only the confirmation.

A page renders the name of the notification section it belongs to as a govuk-caption directly above its heading (govuk-caption-l above heading-l; govuk-caption-xl above the dashboard heading-xl). The map is data (captionSections), not per-page strings: Dashboard | About the consignment (commodity-type, commodities, commodity-details, origin) | Arrival (arrival-status, arrival-details) | Destination (place-of-destination) | Consignment parties (consignor-select, identification-numbers). Overview, both contact pages, check your answers, declaration and confirmation are deliberately bare; the caption test lists the bare pages so a new page needs a decision. Wiring sectionCaption into configureJourneyFlow in routes.js AND test/fixtures/index.js plus the flow/section-captions copy pair is a declared restore extra. Source: live-animals section-captions; skeleton section-captions, section-captions-unwired.

kit.errorSummary builds one govukErrorSummary titled There is a problem with one entry per field error linking to #fieldName (custom href builder when the fix lives on another page, e.g. CYA party errors); the page title is prefixed Error: when a summary is present; field errors render inline via errorMessage; input name, id and error-map key stay identical so the summary link moves focus to the control. Plants answers EVERY validation failure with HTTP 400 — animals is inconsistent (seven pages return 200 with the error page; live-animals note) and that inconsistency is not copied. Source: live-animals error-summary-conventions; skeleton gds-error-wiring.

Every persistence write is wrapped in kit.recoverableSave(): a backend failure classed recoverable re-renders the page with a govukNotificationBanner role=alert (There is a problem: Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.) and HTTP 500, keeping the submitted values; a STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN error redirects to the same URL with ?staleAction=1, which shows The notification has been updated banner. Every form posts a hidden crumb (CSRF) and a hidden concurrencyToken from the loaded journey; the backend mints a new token on each save and rejects a stale one. Source: live-animals recoverable-save, concurrency-and-csrf; skeleton controller-contract, persistence-and-mapper. Serves NNS-UN-009 (complete dependably).

Three journey-scoped cookies, base64json, httpOnly, SameSite Lax, no ttl, named in journeys/linear/config.js and never shared with animals: highRiskPlantsKnownJourneys (ids this session may list/act on), highRiskPlantsOpeningRun (RUN_ACTIVE/RUN_COMPLETE per journey), highRiskPlantsFlowOnlyAnswers (declaration per journey). Registered by registerJourneyCookie and keyed by journey id; they never replace the canonical record. Source: skeleton session-cookies-and-stub-mode (config.js:4-8); live-animals session-cookies.

Radio and select pages validate with oneOf (reject only values outside the offered list) and let a blank answer through so a trader can Save and return with the row still In progress; text inputs validate max length and pattern only. Pages that DO require at page level, copied from animals' split: country of origin (requiredOneOf), the declaration, and collection entry fields at add time (category, and the fields it reveals — mirroring animals' document add fields). Plants additionally requires at page level: commodityType (the entry gate; nothing downstream makes sense without it), arrivalStatus and arrivalDate (the timing rules hang on them). The obligation status, not the page, holds the hub row and the submit gate. Source: live-animals lenient-page-validation (import-reason/controller.js:25); skeleton validation-library.

Two obligations are strictly-earlier prerequisites enforced when the user continues: commodityType and countryOfOrigin (ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE in bridge/obligation-source.js, empty today). Derived page gates hold every later page and section until they are answered and the hub shows Cannot start yet on blocked rows. Mirrors animals' countryOfOrigin + commoditySelection pair. Source: skeleton system-populated-and-enforced-at-continue (obligation-source.js:29-35, prerequisites.js:13-32); live-animals enforced-at-continue.

One org-scoped, typeless address book serves every role (INS-owned, read-only here; writes belong to the INS frontend). The picker page: caption, h1 = party title, description = party hint, a Search input (hint Name, address or country, button Search, action=search re-renders page 1), a results govukTable (Select radio | Name | Address | Country | View details) paginated at 5 per page, No addresses match your search. when empty, and a Selected address: inset. Save commits the id: referenced roles (consignor, placeOfDestination) store { addressId } and resolve details on every read; the inline role (contactAddress) stores a copy { addressId, name, address }. A deleted referenced record renders Not provided and is treated as never entered (the answers-read sanitiser — a restore extra); an outage throws. Organisation id comes only from the verified session, never the payload. Source: live-animals address-book-picker, addresses-hub-page; skeleton addressBook service (address-book/index.js:94-132), answers-read-sanitiser-unwired. Under c-026 and NNS-UN-034 (accurate, structured location).

The dashboard lists the journeys this session knows (cookie ids), scoped to the session organisation (no org -> empty list), excluding DELETED. Left column: Filter notifications (Keyword or reference input, Search). Right column: results label (No Results / Showing 1 Result / Showing {a} to {b} of {n} Results), Sort by (Arrival newest/oldest, Date created newest/oldest; default arrivalDate desc) with Update sort, one govuk-summary-card per notification (title = reference; rows Commodity | Origin | Arrival, Consignor | Status tag (+ Late tag); Date created | Date submitted), per-status actions, pagination, empty text 'You have not started any notifications in this session.', success banners after ?deleted=1 / ?copied=1. Plants swaps the animal-specific cells (Commodity = commodityType + first line category/genus; Arrival = arrivalDate). Source: live-animals dashboard-listing (features/dashboard/controller.js); skeleton dashboardReserved. Provisional pick under c-033.

Dates use the MoJ date picker through kit.dateField: one text box, format d/m/yyyy, width-10, optional min/max as d/m/yyyy text attributes; kit.readDate parses to { day, month, year } (or passes the raw string through so dateText can reject it); stored as the parts object; validated with dateText, or dateTextInRange once a window is ruled (c-029). The journey's bounds helper lives beside the arrival-details feature and returns both validator Dates and picker text from one call. Time (arrivalTime) is a plain HH:MM text input with a new lib/validate factory and default message in both copy files. Source: live-animals date-entry (shared/kit.js:199); skeleton date-fields, validation-library.

Long lists that need type-ahead (countryOfOrigin, genus, proposedPlaceOfLanding) use appAccessibleAutocomplete over a select with showAllValues and a noResults message, listing only a placeholder plus the real options; short fixed lists (commodityType, category, arrivalStatus) are govukRadios with per-option hints. Countries store ISO alpha-2 codes; ports display as {name} ({code}) with value = code; genus stores the SI spelling as the code until a reference service assigns ids. The accessible-autocomplete component already ships under common/components in the plants engine. Source: live-animals select-and-autocomplete-widgets (origin/template.njk:18); skeleton templates-and-nunjucks-roots.

Every plants page extends shared/layout.njk and fills journeyContent only: GOV.UK header linking to gov.uk; govukServiceNavigation with service name Import notification service and, when authenticated, Dashboard | Address book (#) | Manage account (#) | Log out; Alpha phase banner with the feedback mailto; back link when supplied; no breadcrumbs; recoverableError and staleActionRejected banners; journey strip; content in govuk-grid-column-two-thirds for forms and full width for display pages; three-link footer (Privacy | Cookies | Accessibility statement); csrf meta; page title pattern [Error: ]{pageTitle} | Import notification service. Stays inside the govuk-frontend 6.x / MoJ frontend 10.x toolbox — no custom CSS (animals' bespoke hub totals and dashboard classes are debt, not a pattern). Source: skeleton layout-chrome (shared/layout.njk:1-132), shared-chrome-copy; live-animals layout-chrome and the OUTSIDE THE GOVUK TOOLBOX note. Service name, feedback address and the two '#' links are c-032.

Every templated feature owns copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and copy/copy.test.js; controllers call copyFor({ en, cy }) which today always resolves en (no locale toggle, cookie or lang attribute exists in animals or the plants engine); copy-parity.test.js enforces that cy mirrors en path-for-path, kind-for-kind and arity-for-arity and that every string leaf differs from English unless registered in IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST under '<module>:<leafPath>' with a justification (codes, proper nouns, 'GB', reference formats). Every cy file is headed MACHINE-DRAFT Welsh — not reviewed by a translator; the spec copies animals' Welsh only where the English is verbatim animals and invents none. Source: live-animals welsh-copy-seam; skeleton copy-convention, copy-parity, copy-parity-allowlist-key. The Annex 6 requirement for a live Welsh service (annex:6/non-functional/item:7) is the separate open question nfr-english-and-welsh.

Three guards run in routes.js before routes are added, so a partial increment fails the server start, not a test: (1) buildDispatch -> assertFullCoverage throws 'Obligations collected by no page' for any obligation at any depth no page names in collects (via nearest-ancestor ownership) that is not in SYSTEM_POPULATED — the four system obligations (referenceNumber, dateOfNotification, notificationStatus, lateNotificationIndicator) must be listed there or live on the record envelope; (2) createFulfilmentRegistry throws 'obligations owned by no feature' for any unbound leaf and 'must import its obligation object from the manifest' on identity mismatch; (3) assertObligationPurity throws on any label/title/titleKey/hint/legend/widget key in the obligation graph. spec-lint.sh pre-flights guard 1. Every plants obligation therefore lands with its page, its scalar()/grouped() binding and its copy in one increment. Source: skeleton boot-guard-dispatch-coverage, boot-guard-binding-coverage, boot-guard-manifest-identity (dispatch.js:71-90, fulfilment-registry.js:156-163, no-display-keys.js:24-31).

Obligations carry identity, scope, mandate and invariants only — every label, hint, option text and error message in this spec lives in the owning feature's copy pair (the spec's label/hint/errorCopy fields are for the copy pass, never the manifest). applyTo rules are built only from the helper library: equalsGate/includesGate for the notification-level commodityType gates; allowListed(category, <list>, null projection) for the same-frame per-line gates on category; anyAllowListed(category, potatoCategories) if a notification-level rule ever needs to read the lines (the origin narrowing is validation, not applyTo); branchedGate with predicateMeta as the escape hatch. Each allow-list comes from the set-owned commodities service and is pinned by obligations/whitelists.test.js. Source: skeleton model-purity, applyto-helper-vocabulary, helper-selection-rule, obligation-shape (helpers/index.js:32-87, no-display-keys.js:24-31).

copy-convention.test.js and copy-parity.test.js are ARMED against the empty features folder: each asserts readdirSync(features) is [] and fails with a message telling the author to restore the per-feature checks. The first feature increment (dashboard) must, in the same commit, rewrite copy-convention's per-feature half (walk every feature dir, require the copy triple, forbid root-level copy files, check every leaf with isCopyLeaf) and extend copy-parity's modulePairs to every feature's copy/ pair (later plus the flow/section-captions pair), keeping IDENTICAL_ALLOWLIST justified. Declared as two restore extras anchored after the dashboard page. Source: skeleton tripwire-copy-convention, tripwire-copy-parity (copy-convention.test.js:8-27, copy-parity.test.js:16-51).

A collecting controller: one render() helper for GET and POST errors built on kit.base(title, {backLink, journey, page}); GET calls state.get() once and prefills from answers; POST reads raw payload values, validates with lib/validate (service-backed membership rules built INSIDE POST so they see data primed at boot — the category-by-commodityType and origin-by-category narrowings are exactly this), re-renders raw values with status 400 on error, commits cleaned values with state.commit() (never the raw payload), redirects through await kit.nextTarget(request, page, committed.scope); routes = kit.pageRoutes(page, { get, post }). Only obligation names and declared flow-only keys may be committed — helper form fields (index, action, search) are stripped first or assertRecognisedAnswerKeys throws. Every page routes through kit.base so captions and hubHref arrive uniformly (animals' hub/dashboard/CYA controllers that hand-build view models are not copied). Source: skeleton controller-contract, answer-key-recognition, validation-library; live-animals INCONSISTENT chrome assembly note.

commodityLines is the recipe's two-page batch shape: the commodities list page owns the group (collects names only the root), the commodity-details entry sub-page adds one line (appendEntryAt) or edits one by ?index (updateEntryAt after looking the instance up and refusing an index the collection has no entry for), Remove on the list posts remove:<index> (removeEntryAt; Number.isInteger guard), and a leaf-less entry is never persisted. Positions are snapshot-local, never ids. requires.minEntries 1 with errorCode obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne is the floor; there is no sibling-count cap (MAX_ENTRIES_FROM stays empty) and no nested collection. The change context threads through the loop (only the exiting Continue repoints to CYA). Source: skeleton collections-engine-api, cardinality-requires, cardinality-cap, fulfilment-index-tokens; live-animals commodity-batch-search, per-line-cards-and-caps (the search-then-tick and cap machinery are not needed).

Reference data that only makes sense for plants — the three commodityType values, the nine category values and their grouping by type, the fifteen genus entries and the hardwood narrowing, the per-category allow-lists every per-line gate reads, the origin-country narrowing per category — belongs under sets/high-risk-plants/services/commodities as a set-owned service wired through a configure* seam in routes.js, with a stub and (later) a real client, and obligations/whitelists.test.js checking each allow-list against it so a hand-typed list cannot drift. Created by the commodities increment. Policy requires the list to be amendable without a code release (commodity-list-dynamic-and-maintainable) — the service boundary is where that lands. Source: skeleton set-owned-services-seam (docs/services.md); phnns-policy annex:1/closing-para, annex:6/functional/item:4; live-animals STUB-ONLY reference data note (do not copy the name-keyed allow-list vocabulary).

src/server/app/contract.test.js is a manual L1 table pinning that each collecting controller's valid POST commits exactly the committable names in its meta.collects (with any scope seed that brings conditional obligations into scope — e.g. commodityType=potatoes for arrivalTime). The file does not exist; the first plants collecting controller (commodity-type) recreates it and every later collecting page adds a case; only npm test runs it. Declared as a restore extra anchored after commodity-type. Source: skeleton contract-test-table, missing-tests-and-fixtures.

Per feature: controller.test.js (Vitest through the engine with stub services), copy/copy.test.js and a co-located *.fit.spec.js (fit/<page>.fit.spec.js for multi-page groups) that starts its own notification, uses role/label/visible-copy locators imported from copy.en.js, never sleeps, has no page-object layer, and covers initial render, happy-path save and redirect, reload persistence, each validation rule, value preservation on error, every error-summary link moving focus, Back / Save and return / Cancel / Change navigation, conditional scope-skip-purge, CYA rows and Change links, and the hub row states. Accessibility: AxeBuilder withTags wcag2a + wcag2aa on the initial render AND the validation-error state, failing on serious or critical. Set tests: obligations/coverage.test.js (first obligation), whitelists.test.js (first allow-list), flow/task-rows.test.js (first task row). Serves annex:6/non-functional/item:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA) at the page level. Source: skeleton fit-spec-conventions, missing-tests-and-fixtures; live-animals feature-test-conventions.

Every plants increment ends green on, from the repo root: npm run test:high-risk-plants; npm test (pretest builds the frontend; runs the L1 tripwires and the contract table — the only command that does); npm run format:check; npm run lint (eslint neostandard + sonarjs, stylelint gds, depcruise); PORT=3053 npm run test:fit:features; npm run test:fit:journeys when the whole journey or shared FIT helpers change. Green means every command exits 0 with no failed tests and no lint errors; while a suite matches no files, say so rather than reporting coverage. The husky pre-commit hook runs format:check, lint and test. Source: skeleton verification-ladder (package.json:13-50, .husky/pre-commit).

playwright.config.js defines two fit projects against a self-started STUB_MODE server (default port 3003; PORT=3053 when the workspace stack is up): features (every **/*.fit.spec.js under the set) and journeys (fit/journey-smoke.fit.spec.js driven by flow/fixtures/happy-path.json — neither exists). Both pass vacuously today (--pass-with-no-tests). The journeys project stays empty until the journey is walkable end to end, when the smoke spec and the happy-path fixture land together (a restore extra at the end of the backlog); the five mural use cases seed that fixture (use-cases-as-test-fixtures). Deployed multi-service E2E lives in the tests repo as a fourth Playwright project (declared e2e extras). Source: skeleton playwright-projects, tests-repo-plants-project-absent; live-animals feature-test-conventions (fit journeys project).

npm run lint:arch enforces the four layers: only routes.js imports sets/**; L2 (engine/model/bridge/flow/services/lib/shared/analysis) never imports sets; obligations never import journeys; one journey never imports a sibling; sets never import L1; the engine never imports services; the bridge never imports engine/flow/analysis/kit (three bridge->flow violations are baselined in .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json — a declared chore); no circular imports. Plants set code may import L2 APIs and its own set only; a feature that needs the evaluator goes through the engine/bridge. Source: skeleton layer-rules-depcruise (.dependency-cruiser.cjs:13-175), depcruise-known-violations-baselined.

Canonical UUID-keyed fulfilment is the durable answer source: every write replaces a whole evaluated-and-purged snapshot through the records port (create, load, list, has, replaceFulfilment, finalise, amend, cancelAmend, copy, softDelete, clear); reads rebuild projected answers, scope and status so derived state is never stored; one journey load per request. The real adapter derives the backend NotificationDto through notification-mapper/index.js, which today projects referenceNumber and nothing else — the plants backend has no typed content fields, so every plants obligation round-trips through the opaque fulfilments payload. Mapper A only: no Mapper B, no outbox, no event publishing, no PIMS routing, no document upload (epic EUDPA-407). A typed backend field for any plants obligation is a backend-schema decision recorded as an open question, with an explicit omission assertion until then. Source: skeleton persistence-and-mapper (docs/persistence.md, notification-mapper/index.js:1-12).

STUB_MODE is one service-wide switch (refused in production): a stub run serves stub reference data, the stub records/session adapters, and signs its own session via /auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=<org> (default stub-org-1, user STUB0001/2100010101) — auth is still enforced. Real mode uses Defra ID OIDC (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/organisation) and primes countries and ports at boot; /auth/sign-out and the layout's Log out link end the session; auth/unauthorised.njk is the failure view (hardcoded English — a chore). Sign-in is the only precondition to notifying built in this run (c-039). vitest and playwright both set STUB_MODE=true. Source: skeleton session-cookies-and-stub-mode, authSignIn, authSignOut, unauthorised pages.

Prefer server-rendered controls. When a page genuinely needs a client bundle (the accessible-autocomplete on origin, arrival-details and commodity-details already ships as a common component; any add-another or conditional-reveal enhancement beyond govuk radios), put its entry under journeys/linear/features/<name>/client/index.js, add a NAMED entry to the repo-root webpack.config.js, and load it from the template with getAssetPath('<entry>.js'). A missing webpack entry is silent: the page renders, the bundle URL 404s, nothing is logged — build config is load-bearing and the fit spec proves the behaviour. Source: skeleton client-js-webpack (webpack.config.js:22-24, docs/features.md).

Lighthouse CI audits URLs read from .lighthouse/targets.json (npm run lighthouse:targets), desktop preset, signing in first through the Defra ID stub, score floors performance 0.60 / accessibility 0.70 / best-practices 0.70 and NO SEO assertion (none should be added). The URL list is derived from registered routes, so every plants page joins the audit by being reachable after seeding: each needs a stable report name in scripts/lighthouse/audit-targets.js and a seed shape in seed-notification.js that satisfies its prerequisites (a page whose prerequisites are unmet redirects to the hub and silently audits the hub). Both scripts are missing — a fix extra at the start of the backlog — and each page increment adds its seed shape and report name. Source: skeleton lighthouse-expectations, lighthouse-scripts-missing (lighthouserc.cjs:1-54, scripts/lighthouse/).

'Ability to amend the notification before submitting' (annex:6/functional/item:12) and NNS-UN-007 ('confidence that the information I provide is complete and correct ... avoid errors') are met by save-and-return, the hub statuses, inline validation and the Check your answers page with a Change link on every row (cya-change-round-trip). The paper says nothing about amendment after submission — that is notification-actions-after-submission (open question, c-030).

'A decision was made at FTA-TCA group in February 2026 not to charge for these activities as they will be a public good. However, this position will be reviewed once cost data is available (i.e. 2028).' (section:fees-and-charges/para:1). There is no payment step, fee display or invoice reference anywhere in the journey.

The blueprint's Export certification stage reads 'No export cert required' with no actor node (file:blueprint/region:Export certification); the SI matters name no document; epic EUDPA-407 puts document uploads out of this run. The journey must not ask for, require or upload an export certificate, phytosanitary certificate or any other document — no documents collection, no upload page, no document references. Animals' documents feature (0..10 uploads with virus scanning) is not copied. Any later document requirement is document-uploads-out-of-scope (open question).

'Customs dec raised, but no SPS customs hold or matching required' (file:blueprint/region:Customs matching, no actor node). The notification is not matched to a customs declaration and does not hold goods, so the journey collects no customs reference (MRN, entry number) and no transport or port-of-exit details — none of animals' transport section is copied. Failure to notify is detected outside the service by cross-referencing customs and passport data (section:non-compliance/para:1), which is why the supplier, producer and crop identifiers must be matchable values.

'There will instead be a requirement to use EU plant passports, for higher risk material only (mainly plants for planting)' (section:policy/para:1-2). Plant passports are a separate regime: the notification does not ask for, upload or replace passport data. The supplier identification number and EPPO code are the only passport-adjacent values and are typed in, not extracted (import-from-existing-documents is parked).

'Receive information on WHAT is arriving WHEN and WHERE (the notification)' (annex:6/functional/item:1) and NNS-UN-021 (regulator: 'what is arriving, when, and where') are the spine of the journey and the section order: commodity (what) -> origin (where from) -> arrival (when) -> destination (where to) -> parties -> contact -> review. 'Ensure sufficient detail is captured to allow plant health inspectors to identify when spot checks are required' (annex:6/functional/item:3) is why category, genus, origin, destination and date are coded or structured, not free text.

The potato duty (annex:5/reg:24A) and the plants/wood duty (reg 26) are separate regulations with different matters and timing windows, and the mural splits data capture into 'Potatoes (ware and seed)' and 'Other goods' (data-fields-split-by-goods-type). A notification therefore carries exactly one commodityType chosen first; a mixed consignment is two notifications. The commodity-type hint says so. Mirrors animals' inset 'A separate notification is required for each health certificate' in role, not wording.

NNS-UN-010 ('proportionate and relevant so that I only provide information that is necessary for my consignment'), NNS-UN-004 ('simple ... minimal effort' — both bold on the page), NNS-UN-036 (questions depend on consignment status) and NNS-UN-011/013 (potato- and wood-specific sets) are met by scope: every conditional obligation is applyTo on commodityType or category, out-of-scope fields are neither rendered nor validated nor committed, arrival-status is skipped for potatoes, and the derived gates hide a page whose every obligation is out of scope. Article 9(7) OCR caps the data at what is strictly necessary (section:legal-basis/para:1) — no question outside the statutory matters and Common Data is asked. Source: skeleton derived-gates, scope-and-wipe.

'provide written notification to the competent authority of the matters referred to in paragraph (2)' (annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)): the digital submission is the written notification, attributable to the signed-in Defra ID organisation and user, persisted as a SUBMITTED record with a unique reference, the date of notification and the declaration, and retrievable by the authority (NNS-UN-032 traceability). The signed-in organisation is the professional operator; no separate notifier identity is typed (c-038).

The entry page (commodity-type) is the one page whose back link depends on state: hub when the notification already has committed answers, dashboard otherwise. Every other page links back to the hub, except child pages (commodity-details -> commodities; contact-details -> consignment-contact-select) which link to their parent, pages reached with ?change=1 (-> check your answers), the declaration (-> notification-view) and the confirmation (no back link). Source: live-animals origin-back-link, confirmation-page.

'Provide sufficient information for track and trace in the event of an outbreak detection' (annex:6/functional/item:5; section:justification/para:3 traceback/forward). The consignor, supplier identification number, producer and crop identification numbers, country of origin and place of destination / current location are the trace chain and are all captured as required matters; nothing extra is asked. Non-compliance detection cross-references customs, plant-passport and Seed Potato Classification Scheme data (section:non-compliance/para:1), so those identifiers are stored verbatim as entered.

'Examples of potential non-compliances include: Failure to making a notification; Incorrect notification details; Late notification' (section:non-compliance/para:2) with sanctions administered outside the service (section:non-compliance/para:3). A late or post-arrival notification is therefore ACCEPTED and recorded, never blocked: arrivalDate has no future-only rule, the declaration submits regardless of timing, and lateness is a flag (lateNotificationIndicator) shown to the notifier and the authority. The mural use case 'Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification' (file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:2) is a happy-path fixture, not an error case.

The five blueprint use cases (file:blueprint/Use cases/bullet:1-5) — Ware potatoes from Spain/Poland; Ware potatoes from Spain/Portugal with a late notification; Seed potatoes from any EU country; Spruce (Picea) from any EU country; Conifer wood from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain — are the seed shapes for flow/fixtures/happy-path.json, the Lighthouse seed-notification.js SEED_SHAPES and the tests-repo journey specs: one potato pre-arrival, one potato late, one seed potato (origin outside the four ware countries), one plants-for-planting with genus/species/EPPO code, one wood with phytosanitary treatments and the four-country origin narrowing.

Animals is inconsistent: the contact page makes the fieldset legend the page heading (isPageHeading: true) and renders no caption, while every other single-question page renders an h1 plus a legend or label (live-animals note on contact/template.njk:12). Plants picks one convention: a single-question radios page (commodity-type, arrival-status) uses the legend as the page heading with the section caption above it; a single-input page uses an h1 with the label as the heading; the address pickers keep animals' h1 + description. consignment-contact-select stays exactly as animals (same-as-animals) — its bare, legend-as-heading shape is the source of the plants convention.

Stay in the govuk-frontend toolbox: Nunjucks macros from govuk-frontend 6.x and @ministryofjustice/frontend 10.x, govuk-* utility classes, the shipped accessible-autocomplete component; no hand-rolled components or custom CSS. Animals' bespoke classes (app-commodity-total*, notification-list__*, app-link-button, app-form-inline) and its custom hub totals panel are debt and are not copied; the plants dashboard cards and hub use govukSummaryCard and govukTaskList as-is. Source: live-animals OUTSIDE THE GOVUK TOOLBOX note; skeleton templates-and-nunjucks-roots; annex:6/non-functional/item:2 'Meets GDS standards'.

services/import-reason-purpose serves nothing (both label maps are {} — 'Deliberately empty. The journey's import reasons and purposes are not yet agreed') and has no real client. No plants source asks a reason-for-import or purpose question — the potato 'intended use' and the optional 'use' are free-text per-line matters — so the plants journey does not use this service and the platform's transport-reference and commercial-transporters services are likewise unused. Whether to delete or keep them is a declared chore at the start of the backlog. Source: skeleton import-reason-purpose-empty, importReasonPurpose/transportReference/commercialTransporters serviceOnly fields.

'New SPS rules on GOV.UK and Europa.EU' is the Guidance & comms stage (file:blueprint/region:Guidance & comms, actor Importer, agent) — guidance is published outside the service. NNS-UN-001 (understand whether my goods are high-risk and pre/post), NNS-UN-002 and NNS-UN-008 (understand what information is required, first time right) are met inside the journey by the dashboard intro copy, a GOV.UK guidance link, the commodity-type option hints (timing windows) and per-field hint text, not by separate guidance or before-you-start pages. A dedicated eligibility checker ('are my goods high-risk?') is the open question guidance-before-you-start.

Potatoes: 'at least two days before the expected date of their arrival' (section:policy/para:6/item:1; annex:5/reg:24A(1)); plants and wood: 'before or no later than four days after the date of their arrival' (section:policy/para:6/item:2; reg 26(1)); 'Highlight to the user (internal and external) when a notification was made outside of required timings' (annex:6/functional/item:2); NNS-UN-012 (importer told when late and what rule) and NNS-UN-014 (regulator sees late ones). Actor: importer and regulator. Proposed: submitJourney computes lateNotificationIndicator from arrivalDate, commodityType and dateOfNotification in Europe/London (potatoes: late if submitted after arrivalDate minus 2 days; plants/wood: late if submitted more than 4 days after arrivalDate; a future date is never late), stores it on the record, and the confirmation/CYA read-only view shows a banner naming the rule. Open: whether 'two days before' is calendar days or 48 hours; whether the potato time of arrival counts; whether to warn on CYA before submission (c-035); whether the engine exposes a derived-at-submit hook or the backend computes it. Conflicts c-002, c-029, c-031, c-035.

NNS-UN-001, NNS-UN-025 ('pre-nots' / 'post-nots') and NNS-UN-036 treat pre/post-movement status as something the importer must understand and that drives what is asked; the page never says whether the importer chooses it or the service derives it from the arrival date (annex:5/reg:26(2)(a)-(b) phrase it as either/or). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-006): a user-selected arrivalStatus radios page for plants and wood before the date and destination pages; potatoes have no status (c-002). Alternative: derive from arrivalDate being past or future (ambiguous on the day of arrival, and would reorder the arrival section). Gate question.

The draft SI is England-only ('into England', 'arrival in England', 'landing in England' — annex:5/reg:24A(1), reg:26(1)-(2)(a)) but reg 26(2)(b) says 'intended destination in Great Britain', the Policy section says 'arrival in GB', the user needs say 'imports into Great Britain' and the mural says 'EU -> GB'; Scottish Government is a competent authority (section:policy/para:7) and NNS-UN-029 wants Scottish regulators to see consignments in their region, yet nothing says how a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified. Actor: importer, policy. Proposed (c-001): 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading, arrivalDate labels, hint copy) and no territorial validation on the destination address. Open: whether the SI will be widened to GB, or the service must route Scottish destinations elsewhere.

The origin country list is constrained by what is being imported: ware potatoes only Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain (annex:5/reg:24A(1)(b)) with Spain excluding the Balearic Islands (reg 24A(3)); seed potatoes any part of the Common SPS Area other than the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man (reg 24A(1)(a)); plants for planting 'grown in, or from, a member State'; wood 'from a member State' except conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain only (reg 26(1)); the mural narrows ware potatoes to Spain and Poland (c-021). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-022): countryOfOrigin stays same-as-animals (autocomplete, always in scope, one obligation) over an EU-member-state block; the narrowing is validation inside POST from the set-owned commodities service, keyed on the categories present in commodityLines (the engine shape would be anyAllowListed); 'Spain (excluding the Balearic Islands)' is hint text. Open: whether an out-of-scope origin (ware potatoes from France) should be rejected, warned, or accepted as a notification the scheme does not require; whether the country block for plants is GBNAG_SPS_EX or a new one; whether a region option is needed for Spain.

category is always in scope on every line (no scope gate), so scope-and-wipe cannot purge lines whose category no longer belongs to a changed commodityType (skeleton scope-and-wipe, helper-selection-rule: a value-list mismatch is not a scope condition). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-013): the commodities list page reconciles on load — lines whose category is outside the new type's set are dropped with a notification banner — mirroring animals' reconcile-by-key on the search page (reconcileEntriesAt). Alternative: three typed collections (potatoLines, plantLines, woodLines) each gated on commodityType with wipeOnExit so the model does the wiping, at the cost of three collection pages and duplicated quantity fields. Alternative: retain lines and let validation flag them (NNS-UN-006 'flexible'). Gate question; a candidate model extension if Sam wants the model to own it.

Animals bounds its arrival date to [today - 7 days, today + 6 months] (live-animals arrival.js:5, dateTextInRange, one clock read per request). No plants source gives a bound; the timing rules only define lateness and a late notification must be accepted (late-accepted-not-rejected; mural use case bullet:2). Actor: importer. Proposed (c-029): dateText only (a real calendar date), no window, lateness derived at submission. Open: a sanity window to catch typos (for example 1 year back to 1 year ahead), whether a potato date in the past should trigger an 'already arrived' question the SI does not have, and whether the picker should carry min/max attributes at all.

The plants backend ReferenceNumberGenerator and the frontend stub adapter mint {YY}-{XXXXXX} with no type-code prefix, both flagged PENDING REQUIREMENTS; animals uses GBN-AG-; referenceNumber has a unique index so the prefix must be decided before real data exists (skeleton reference-number-format, backend-reference-prefix-absent; annex:6/generated-data/item:1). The plants type code is an open question on epic EUDPA-407. Actor: policy, backend. Proposed (c-023): a gated cross-repo fix extra (backend generator + REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN + tests; frontend stub + any display copy) anchored before the confirmation page, blocked until the code is agreed; the journey strip, dashboard and confirmation show whatever the backend mints meanwhile.

'Notification status' is generated data with no vocabulary (annex:6/generated-data/item:3); the engine and animals carry DRAFT / SUBMITTED / AMEND / DELETED; NNS-UN-020 wants compliance to be 'a reportable status rather than an inference'; policy expects checks, results and non-compliances to attach to the notification (annex:6/functional/item:8-9). Actor: regulator, importer. Proposed (c-024): notificationStatus = the engine lifecycle; lateness as a separate flag; check outcomes are inspector-side data that never change the importer-facing status in this run. Open: whether policy wants a richer status (Late, Selected for check, Checked, Non-compliant) visible to the importer, and what the dashboard tag should read.

Animals offers per-status dashboard actions (SUBMITTED: View, Amend, Copy as new, Delete; DRAFT: Resume, Copy as new, Delete; AMEND: Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete) with cancel-amend and delete confirmation pages, and the plants engine already reserves the amend/cancel-amend/copy/delete slugs and records-port operations (skeleton actionSlugsReserved). The policy paper covers only amend-before-submitting and 'says nothing about amending a notification after submission, cancelling one, what happens if the consignment does not arrive'; the user needs are silent except NNS-UN-041 (reuse = Copy as new, parked). Actor: importer, regulator. Proposed (c-030): no cancel-amend or delete PAGE in the spec; the dashboard shows Resume and View only until ruled; Amend, Copy as new and Delete are gate questions because a submitted notification is a statutory record the regulator may have acted on (spot-check scheduled). If ruled in, the two confirmation pages are copied from animals as chores anchored after the confirmation page.

The mural names the service 'High risk Plants EU -> GB (PHNNS)' and leaves Support 'TBC' (file:blueprint/left header card, region:Support); the engine's chrome carries the animals service name 'Import notification service', the APHA service-desk feedback mailto, '#' Address book and Manage account links and an English-only unauthorised view (skeleton chrome-hardcoded-and-placeholder-links); animals' confirmation help block names the APHA live-animals mailboxes; competent authorities for plants are APHA, the Forestry Commission and Scottish Government (section:policy/para:7). Actor: importer, service owner. Proposed (c-032): keep the shared chrome verbatim; the confirmation help block says 'contact the plant health authority' with no invented address; a gated chore resolves the feedback address, the two placeholder links and the unauthorised view copy. Open: the plants helpdesk, whether the service name changes for plants, and where Address book / Manage account live (INS front door).

countries.prime() fetches /countries?blocks=GBNAG_SPS_EX (the animals SPS origin block) and the capture script records the stub fixture with the same block; reference-data marks /ports-of-entry as 'expected — endpoint not built' so the ports stub fixture may be a placeholder (skeleton countries-block-and-capture-coupling, ports serviceOnly field). Plants needs an EU-member-state origin list (origin-value-list-by-commodity) and a place-of-landing list for potatoes only (c-020). Actor: reference-data owner. Proposed: a gated fix extra before the origin page — name the plants country block (or confirm GBNAG_SPS_EX), re-run npm run capture:high-risk-plants, update the countries stub and run-mode.test.js; confirm whether proposedPlaceOfLanding can use /ports-of-entry or needs a landing-place list of its own.

NNS-UN-001 ('understand whether my goods are high-risk and subject to a pre or post-movement notification'), NNS-UN-002 and NNS-UN-008 ('understand what information is required ... prepare correctly / correctly first time') imply an up-front eligibility check and a before-you-start list; the mural puts guidance on GOV.UK and Europa.EU outside the service (file:blueprint/region:Guidance & comms) and the policy commodity list is dynamic (annex:1/closing-para). Actor: importer. Proposed (guidance-link-not-in-journey-pages): no eligibility or before-you-start page in this run — the dashboard intro links to GOV.UK guidance and the commodity-type hints name the windows. Open: whether the service should host an 'Is my consignment high-risk?' checker driven by the same set-owned commodities service, which would be a new start-section page. Parked, not rejected.

'Following receipt of a notification, the relevant competent authority (APHA, FC or Scottish Government) will undertake random spot checks at destination' (section:policy/para:7); 'Provides Defra Policy, Scottish Government and Forestry Commission with the same level of access to the data in the system as APHA' (annex:6/functional/item:11); NNS-UN-029 (Scottish region) and NNS-UN-030 (Forestry Commission sees wood). Actor: regulator, backend. Proposed: the notifier journey collects enough to route — commodityType (wood -> FC), placeOfDestination (region -> SG) — and does nothing else; routing, access parity and region derivation from the address are backend and internal-side open questions outside this frontend. The journey shows no 'your notification has been sent to X' copy.

PARKED, not rejected. 'Provide the option to bulk upload (external) to or download data (internal) from the system' (annex:6/functional/item:6); NNS-UN-005 ('submit notifications for large shipments efficiently ... high volumes of consignments') — format, scope and whether it means many notifications at once are unstated (c-040). Actor: importer. Out of this run per the brief; the many-lines reading is met by commodityLines. When picked up it is an alternative entry route (a file page in the start section) that must produce the same canonical fulfilment as the form.

PARKED, not rejected. NNS-UN-042: 'import consignment information from existing documents so that I don't have to manually input the same data' — documents and format unstated (invoice, plant passport, phytosanitary certificate?). Actor: importer. Out of this run per the brief and because document uploads are out per epic EUDPA-407 (document-uploads-out-of-scope). Would need an upload-and-extract route feeding the same obligations.

PARKED, not rejected. NNS-UN-041: 'reuse previously entered consignment information so that I don't have to input the same data repeatedly'; Annex 6 'Minimise effort and potential disruption to traders' (annex:6/non-functional/item:10). Actor: importer. Animals meets the same need with Copy as new (a DRAFT copy of a submitted notification opened at the hub) and the engine already exposes records.copy (skeleton actionSlugsReserved). Out of this run per the brief; ruled together with notification-actions-after-submission (c-030). The prototype's templates feature (manageTemplates) is a second pattern for the same need.

PARKED, not rejected. NNS-UN-039: 'I need an agent to act on my behalf so that I can so that I can ensure my notification obligations are fulfilled' (duplicated phrase verbatim); the mural names the actor 'Importer, agent' at every importer-facing stage; the SI puts the duty on the professional operator (c-038). How the agent is identified, authorised or linked, and whether the agent needs their own registration, is unstated. Actor: importer, agent. Out of this run per the brief (agent authorisation). In this run the signed-in Defra ID organisation is the notifier and the declaration carries the third-party clause copied from animals; no agent party is collected.

PARKED, not rejected. NNS-UN-038: 'register myself as a plant operator so that I can notify authorities' — highlighted orange on the page with no legend; the mural Setup actions stage 'Register for new [GB product] — Importer, agent' with the product in placeholder brackets (file:blueprint/region:Setup actions); the policy is silent on external sign-in (c-039). Actor: importer. Out of this run per the brief; Defra ID sign-in is the only precondition built. If ruled in it is an onboarding step or a registration check before the dashboard, outside the notification journey.

PARKED, not rejected — out of the notifier journey per the brief. Regulator needs: NNS-UN-014 (late notifications), NNS-UN-015 (incoming high-risk plants), NNS-UN-016 (high-quality data to prioritise), NNS-UN-017 (trust accuracy and consistency), NNS-UN-018 (reuse across reporting), NNS-UN-020 (whether mandatory notifications were met), NNS-UN-021 (what, when, where), NNS-UN-024 (inspection team: all consignments visible at volume), NNS-UN-029 (Scottish Government: my region), NNS-UN-030 (Forestry Commission: wood), NNS-UN-031 (inspection frequency per commodity), NNS-UN-032 (trace outcomes back to the notification); policy annex:6/functional/item:9 (view consignment data, PQs and correspondence). Actor: regulator, inspection team. What the notifier journey owes them: coded category/genus/country, structured destination with a region, arrival date, the late flag, a stable reference — all captured. The screens themselves are another product (the mural's Case management stage records outcomes in '[TBC]').

PARKED, not rejected — out of the notifier journey per the brief. Inspector needs: NNS-UN-022 (accurate, timely data), NNS-UN-023 (detailed characteristics), NNS-UN-025 (location or intended destination by pre/post), NNS-UN-028 (risk level), NNS-UN-033 (record a consignment that was not notified — highlighted orange, meaning unstated), NNS-UN-037 (record inspection outcomes and findings); policy annex:6/functional/item:8 (data to scheduling systems and results back), section:legal-basis/para:3/item:5 (written records of checks), Reporting metric 'Attempted checks unable to be completed as commodity moved on'. Actor: inspector. The notifier journey owes them arrivalStatus + placeOfDestination (current location when already arrived) and the contact details; outcome capture, non-notified records and risk level live inspector-side.

PARKED, not rejected — out of the notifier journey per the brief. NNS-UN-027 (Data Analyst: use my data outside the service), NNS-UN-018 (regulator: reuse across reporting), policy 'download data (internal)' (annex:6/functional/item:6), 'Data will need to be extracted from the system for reporting and evaluation purposes ... does not have to necessarily come directly from the PHNNS digital solution' (section:reporting-requirements/para:1,4) and the mural's Reporting stage 'CDS data pulled into TDS2 (datalake) for reporting' (file:blueprint/region:Reporting). Actor: Data Analyst, Defra and ALB reporting users. The notifier journey owes structured, reportable values; the export itself is backend/datalake work.

PARKED, not rejected — out of the notifier journey per the brief. 'The list will be dynamic and subject to risk based changes ... the digital solution will need to include the functionality to enable the list to be amended' (annex:1/closing-para; section:policy/para:4); 'Allow easy maintenance of Commodities in scope; Genus & species in scope; Risk related spot check %' (annex:6/functional/item:4/sub:1-3); 'Variable percentage checks across different commodities ... flexibility to change those % checks' (section:risk-basis/para:1/item:1-2); NNS-UN-019 (risk classifications aligned with current policy); footnotes 2-3 (Juglans and Pterocarya already removed once). Actor: regulator, policy. What this run owes it: the commodityType, category, genus and origin lists live in a set-owned service behind a seam, never hard-coded in obligations or copy, so a list change is a data change (set-owned-commodities-service). The admin surface is another product.

PARKED, not rejected — out of the notifier journey per the brief. 'random spot checks at destination using a risk based process on a percentage of notified commodities ... at an appropriate time to ensure the pest(s) of concern can be detected' (section:policy/para:7); checks are non-discriminatory, risk-based, generally without prior notice, with written records (section:legal-basis/para:3/item:1-5); PHNNS checks are additional to existing surveillance (section:policy/para:8); 'Provide data to operational solutions used to schedule and execute any checks' (annex:6/functional/item:8) and the alpha question of which scheduling systems (annex:6/alpha-questions). Actor: APHA caseworker, inspector, competent authority. Consequence for this journey: NO 'check booked' step, no appointment, no notice to the trader; the confirmation says a check may happen at the destination without notice.

PARKED per epic EUDPA-407 (document uploads out of this run). No plants source lists a document (no-export-certificate-or-documents; the SI matters name none); NNS-UN-042 wants document IMPORT (parked separately). The engine's persistence notes 'no document upload' and Mapper A only (skeleton persistence-and-mapper). Actor: importer. Animals' documents collection (0..10 uploads, cdp-uploader, virus-scan polling) is the shape to copy if a document requirement ever appears; nothing is built now.

PARKED per epic EUDPA-407 (outbox and GBN-AG event publishing out of this run). The plants engine's real records adapter derives a NotificationDto with no typed content fields and no outbox, PIMS routing or event publishing (skeleton persistence-and-mapper: 'Mapper A only'). Policy needs the submitted notification to reach operational scheduling systems and inspectors live (annex:6/functional/item:8,10; NNS-UN-022) — that hand-off is backend and gateway work outside this frontend. Actor: backend, dynamics-gateway. The journey's only obligation is a synchronous submitJourney that persists the whole snapshot.

PARKED per epic EUDPA-407 (a combined animals+plants list in INS out of this run). The prototype's Design release 2 dashboard anticipated a cross-journey 'By type' filter (Live animals / Plants / Products of animal origin) and a 'Plants' card label; Design release 2.1 withdrew it (prototype dashboard-type-filter-plants-placeholder, dashboard-card-plants-category-label-demo; c-033). Actor: importer, INS. The plants dashboard lists plants notifications only (dashboard-listing); the INS front door owns any cross-journey list later.

'The digital solution will need to enable monitoring of the following: Number of notifications (by country and commodity); Number of checks (by country and commodity); % checks for each commodity; Number of non-compliances (pests/other); Summary of action taken following non-compliance; Time taken per notification; Time taken for spot checks; Attempted checks unable to be completed as commodity moved on' (section:reporting-requirements/para:3/item:1-8); 'Facilitate management information and report generation' (annex:6/functional/item:7). Actor: Defra policy, reporting users. What the notifier journey owes the eight: countryOfOrigin as an ISO code and category/genus as coded values (metrics 1-3); dateOfNotification plus a created-at timestamp on the record for 'time taken per notification' (metric 6 — the engine records created/submitted dates on the envelope, mirrored from animals' Date created | Date submitted); metrics 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 are inspector-side data. Open: whether 'time taken' means wall-clock from create to submit or something the journey must measure.

'Enables live access for APHA inspectors to data in the system' (annex:6/functional/item:10) and NNS-UN-022 ('accurate and timely data') mean a submitted notification is visible to inspectors immediately — no batch hand-off. Actor: inspector, backend. The frontend side is already synchronous (submitJourney -> records.finalise -> SUBMITTED before the confirmation renders); whether the plants backend exposes the record to inspector tooling live is a backend question (outbox-and-gbnag-publishing-out-of-scope).

'Provides Defra Policy, Scottish Government and Forestry Commission with the same level of access to the data in the system as APHA' (annex:6/functional/item:11; section:summary/para:4 'APHA, Forestry Commission and Scottish Government will need access to the scheme'). Actor: internal users across four organisations. Internal access is multi-organisation with parity — organisation-aware users, no organisation-scoped data restriction — and is wholly outside the notifier frontend, which scopes only the importer's own notifications to their Defra ID organisation.

'System is accessible (WCAG2.2AA)' (annex:6/non-functional/item:1). Actor: service owner. Covered per page by the fit-spec axe checks (wcag2a + wcag2aa on initial and error states, serious/critical fail) and the Lighthouse accessibility floor 0.70 (feature-test-conventions-and-axe, lighthouse-audit-per-page); axe tags cover WCAG 2.1, so the 2.2-specific criteria (focus appearance, target size, dragging, consistent help, redundant entry, accessible authentication) need a manual audit and an accessibility statement — neither exists in animals or the skeleton. Open: who owns the WCAG 2.2 audit and the statement the footer links to.

'Meets GDS standards' (annex:6/non-functional/item:2). Actor: service owner. The journey uses the GOV.UK Design System through govuk-frontend 6.x only (govuk-toolbox-only), one thing per page for single-question pages, check-your-answers, confirmation panel, error summary conventions and the Alpha phase banner. Open: the Service Standard assessment itself (alpha/beta), which the mural marks 'Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required' (file:blueprint sticky) — outside the codebase.

'Meets GDPR requirements' (annex:6/non-functional/item:3). Actor: service owner, data protection. Personal data in the notification: contactAddress (name of the person making the entry), contactNumber, contactEmail, consignor name and address, the Defra ID user. The paper specifies no lawful basis, privacy notice or retention period, and 'says nothing about record retention periods'. The layout footer's Privacy link is an animals placeholder. Open: privacy notice content and URL, retention of submitted notifications and drafts, and whether the address-book copy semantics (inline copy of the contact) create a second copy of personal data to govern.

'System is secure (userid & password to access for internal users)' (annex:6/non-functional/item:4); the paper says nothing about how external notifiers sign in. Actor: internal users, importer. The notifier frontend already enforces Defra ID OIDC sign-in (stub-mode-and-sign-in) and org-scoped data; internal userid/password access is another product. Open: whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity (the mural's 'Register for new [GB product]' hints at a registration the SI does not require).

'Available 24x7' (annex:6/non-functional/item:6) — timing windows are counted in days against arrival so a notifier must be able to submit at any hour; NNS-UN-009 (complete dependably whenever required); NNS-UN-026 (service owner: usable and reliable under varying demand); the mural sizes the service at 59k notifications a year, 26% of plant imports, with seasonal peaks implied (file:blueprint/left header card). Actor: service owner. Infrastructure, performance testing (k6) and the CDP platform SLA are outside the journey; the journey's contribution is save-and-return, recoverable-save banners and no long synchronous work at submit. Open: peak-load targets and the k6 suite for plants.

'Available in English & Welsh language' (annex:6/non-functional/item:7). Actor: importer, Welsh Language Standards. The copy seam (copyFor, copy.cy.js per feature, copy-parity) is adopted from animals (welsh-copy-seam) and every same-as-animals string carries the animals Welsh, but NO runtime locale toggle exists in animals or the plants engine (copyFor always resolves en), every cy file is machine-draft, and this spec invents no Welsh — variant and plants-only copy has no Welsh at all. Open: the locale switch (cookie / lang query / Defra ID preference), translator review before any Welsh ships, and whether English-only is acceptable for the first release.

'Standardise information as much as is possible' (annex:6/non-functional/item:8); NNS-UN-016/017 (coded, consistent values); NNS-UN-006 pulls the other way ('detailed and flexible product information'). Actor: regulator, importer. Coded in this spec: commodityType, category, genus, countryOfOrigin, proposedPlaceOfLanding, arrivalStatus, notificationStatus; free text because no source gives a list: species, commodityCode, quantity (unit), potatoVariety, potatoIntendedUse, eppoCode, sizeOfTree, phytosanitaryTreatments, use, the three identification numbers, consignmentNumber (c-011). Open: which of those policy wants as controlled lists (intended use options, treatment codes such as HT/KD, a variety register, EPPO code lookup) and who supplies them.

'Include means of data validation' (annex:6/non-functional/item:9); NNS-UN-007 (confidence the information is complete and correct); NNS-UN-017 (trust accuracy). Actor: importer, regulator. Every element has a rule in this spec — membership for coded values, real-date for dates, whole number for quantity, max length for text — but NO format rule exists for any free-text element because no source gives one (c-011). Open: formats for commodity code (tariff scheme), EPPO code, the three identification numbers, contact number and email, arrival time; each is a new lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files once ruled.

'Minimise effort and potential disruption to traders' (annex:6/non-functional/item:10); 'The efficiency of the scheme, to show it is not overly onerous to trade' (section:reporting-requirements/para:2/item:2); NNS-UN-004 ('simple ... minimal effort', bold on the page); Article 9(7) OCR caps data at what is strictly necessary. Actor: importer, policy. Met in this run by: only the statutory matters plus Common Data are asked; scope hides irrelevant questions; save-and-return; address-book picks instead of typed addresses. Open and parked: reuse-previous-consignment, bulk-upload, import-from-existing-documents — the three effort-savers the needs ask for. The 'time taken per notification' MI metric measures this.

'Sustainable' (annex:6/non-functional/item:5) — unqualified; no journey-level consequence stated by any source. Actor: service owner. Recorded so the Annex 6 list is complete; nothing in the spec depends on it. Open: what policy means (environmental, financial, maintainable).

Wood scope conditions: conifer wood with bark or isolated bark from any member State; conifer wood without bark only from Italy, France, Portugal and Spain; cut coniferous trees only when greater than 3 metres in height; wood of Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only when it retains its natural round surface or is in unprocessed chips; preservative-treated wood excluded from every item except cut trees (annex:5/reg:26(1)(b)(i)-(iv); h4:Additional caveats for wood products/li:1-4; file:data-fields/region:Wood/bullet:1-4). Actor: wood importer (NNS-UN-013). Proposed (c-007): the category values encode the item and its form; preservative treatment, the 3-metre threshold and the bark condition are hint and guidance copy, not questions — a wood importer whose consignment is outside scope simply does not notify. Open: whether policy wants explicit pre-scope questions ('Is the wood preservative-treated?') so out-of-scope consignments are caught, and whether an out-of-scope answer should end the journey with a 'you do not need to notify' page.

Seed potatoes are in scope 'grown or suspected of having been grown in another part of the Common SPS Area, other than in the United Kingdom, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man' (annex:5/reg:24A(1)(a); mural use case 'Seed potatoes from any EU country'); ware potatoes only from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain (reg 24A(1)(b)) where 'Spain' excludes the Balearic Islands (reg 24A(3)); the mural says Spain and Poland with an off-board footnote (c-021). Actor: potato importer (NNS-UN-011). Proposed: the seed/ware split is the per-line category, the origin narrowing is validation (origin-value-list-by-commodity), and 'excluding the Balearic Islands' is hint text on the origin page when a ware-potato line exists. Open: 'suspected of having been grown' — whether the notifier must declare suspicion; a region-level origin option for Spain; the mural footnote.

'The information captured by PHNSS will be the same as was required under the previous notification system but with some additional requirements (see annex 2)' (section:policy/para:5; section:general-questions/para:1/item:1) and 'Similar notification systems are used in Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland' (section:summary/para:6; section:legal-basis/para:1). Actor: design research, policy. No extractor could read the previous scheme's form or the NI/RoI services; they are precedents for page copy, the 'intended use' options and the identification-number formats this spec lacks. Open: obtain the pre-2021 national notification scheme's data list and the NI/RoI screens as a design input before the copy pass.

'The PHNNS has been identified as a day 1 critical need' for when the SPS agreement enters into force (section:summary/para:5; section:legal-basis/para:4) — no date given; the document is Version 1 August 2026 with draft SI text, so the statutory wording, the commodity list and the timing windows are all subject to change (docProps:core; annex:1/closing-para); the mural blueprint is 'Alpha Phase Confirmed - Update as Required'. Actor: delivery, policy. Consequence for the build: every list is data behind the set-owned service; every window is one constant in the lateness derivation; the England/GB strings are copy leaves — so a policy change is a data or copy change, not a model change. Open: the go-live date and who re-runs the digest when the paper is reissued.

'In general checks should be carried out without prior notice' and selection is a non-discriminatory, risk-based draw (section:legal-basis/para:3/item:1-4); the mural's Checks stage is 'Risk-based spot checks done at-destination — APHA caseworker / inspector' (file:blueprint/region:Checks). The notifier journey has no 'check booked' step, no appointment slot, no inspection date and no notice; the confirmation page says only that a check may take place at the place of destination without prior notice. Policy also notes a post-arrival notifier may give a current location instead of the destination, so a check may happen elsewhere than first notified — that is why arrivalStatus + placeOfDestination are captured together.
